title: Networking Basics (OSI, TCP/IP)
desc: OSI & TCP/IP models, network devices, IP vs MAC addresses and ports.
objectives: Explain what a network is and name the main network devices
Describe the seven OSI layers and the four TCP/IP layers
Explain encapsulation and the PDU name used at each layer
Tell MAC addresses, IP addresses and port numbers apart
Recognise private and public IPv4 addresses

lessons.title: IP addresses, MAC addresses and ports

title: IP Addressing & Subnetting
desc: Binary, CIDR, subnet masks and step-by-step subnetting.
objectives: Convert between binary and decimal
Read and write subnet masks and CIDR prefixes
Calculate the network address, broadcast address and usable host range
Divide a network into equal subnets
Check your answers with the Subnet Calculator

title: Basic Routing & Static Routes
desc: Routing tables, static and default routes, Longest Prefix Match.
objectives: Read a routing table and understand its route codes
Configure static and default routes on a Cisco router
Explain why a return route is always needed
Apply the Longest Prefix Match rule
Practise in the Packet Walk and Router Lab tools

lessons.title: Static routes and the default route

title: Switching, VLANs & Trunking
desc: How switches forward frames, VLAN segmentation and 802.1Q trunks.
objectives: Explain how a switch learns MAC addresses and forwards frames
Describe what a VLAN is and why networks use them
Configure access ports and trunk ports
Understand 802.1Q tagging and inter-VLAN routing
Recognise common VLAN problems

title: Dynamic Routing (RIP, OSPF)
desc: How routers learn routes automatically and choose the best path.
objectives: Explain the difference between static and dynamic routing
Describe how RIP works and where it falls short
Describe how OSPF builds a map of the network
Compare metrics and administrative distance
Read basic routing protocol output

title: Network Services (DHCP, DNS, NAT)
desc: The services that make real networks and the Internet usable.
objectives: Explain how DHCP gives a device an address
Describe how DNS turns names into IP addresses
Explain how NAT and PAT share public addresses
Troubleshoot basic service problems
Understand where these services fit in a network
